title: From a basis, suffering arises. All the various sufferings in the world arise from a basis. The fool, because of ignorance, creates the basis, Thus…
content:
From a basis, suffering arises.
All the various sufferings in the world arise from a basis.
The fool, because of ignorance, creates the basis,
Thus repeatedly encountering suffering.
Therefore, a wise person should not create a basis,
Contemplating the existence of birth and suffering.

Those who fall into the round of birth and death,
Going from this existence to that existence,
Their destination is due to ignorance.

This great ignorance leads to long wandering.
Beings who have attained true knowledge go no further.

title: Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: - Venerable Sir, is there anything that, being born, does not age…
content:
Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: - Venerable Sir, is there anything that, being born, does not age and does not die?
- Great King, there is nothing that, being born, does not age and does not die. Great King, even those wealthy nobles, rich, with great wealth and property, with abundant gold and silver, abundant goods and grains — they, being born, are not free from aging and death.

title: Standing to one side, that devata spoke this verse before the Blessed One: 'Those who regarding phenomena, Do not thoroughly understand them, Are led astray,…
content:
Standing to one side, that devata spoke this verse before the Blessed One:

'Those who regarding phenomena,
Do not thoroughly understand them,
Are led astray,
Wandering among various sects.
They sleep on and on,
They are not awake,
Now indeed it is time
For them to awaken.'

( Blessed One ):
'Those who regarding phenomena,
Thoroughly understand them with wisdom,
Are not led astray,
Wandering among various sects,
They have attained perfect enlightenment.
They fully understand perfectly,
On the uneven path,
They walk evenly.'

title: - Bhikkhus, when a turban or head is on fire, what should be done?" - "Venerable Sir, when a turban or head is on fire,…
content: - Bhikkhus, when a turban or head is on fire, what should be done?" - "Venerable Sir, when a turban or head is on fire, to extinguish the burning turban or head, one should arouse extraordinary desire, effort, exertion, energy, without backsliding, with mindfulness and clear comprehension." - "Leaving aside the burning turban or head, bhikkhus, for the sake of truly realizing the Four Noble Truths that have not yet been realized, one should arouse extraordinary desire, effort, exertion, energy, without backsliding, with mindfulness and clear comprehension. What four? The Noble Truth of Suffering ... the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering. Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is suffering.' ... an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'

title: - Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who are endowed with virtue, endowed with concentration, endowed with wisdom, endowed with liberation, endowed with knowledge and vision of liberation…
content: - Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who are endowed with virtue, endowed with concentration, endowed with wisdom, endowed with liberation, endowed with knowledge and vision of liberation — I say that seeing those bhikkhus brings great benefit. Hearing those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Paying homage to those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Associating with those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Remembering those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Following those bhikkhus into homelessness, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, when hearing the Dhamma from such bhikkhus, one lives in seclusion, with two kinds of seclusion: seclusion of body and seclusion of mind. One who lives in seclusion thus will recollect that Dhamma and reflect on that Dhamma.

title: Whatever beings, bhikkhus, in the morning do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good morning. Whatever…
content: Whatever beings, bhikkhus, in the morning do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good morning. Whatever beings, bhikkhus, at noon do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good noon. Whatever beings, bhikkhus, in the evening do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good evening.

title: One who has seen the supreme, And heard the unsurpassed, Gained the unsurpassed, Delights in the unsurpassed training, Established in service, Develops the specific recollections,…
content:
One who has seen the supreme,
And heard the unsurpassed,
Gained the unsurpassed,
Delights in the unsurpassed training,
Established in service,
Develops the specific recollections,
Connected to seclusion,
Attains security, the Deathless,
Joyful, not heedless,
Careful, guarding virtue,
When the time has ripened,
Suffering is destroyed.

title: - Just as a great crowd of people, bhikkhus, would gather together and say: 'The national beauty! The national beauty!' And that national beauty, with…
content: - Just as a great crowd of people, bhikkhus, would gather together and say: 'The national beauty! The national beauty!' And that national beauty, with all her charms, would dance for them, with all her charms, would sing for them. And an even larger crowd would gather and say: 'The national beauty dances and sings.' Then a man would come who wants to live, not to die, who wants happiness and loathes suffering. They would say to him: 'Friend, look here. This is a bowl filled with oil. You must carry this bowl of oil through the great crowd and the national beauty. And a man with a drawn sword will follow behind you. Wherever you spill even a little of the oil, there your head will fall.' What do you think, bhikkhus, would that man, not attending to the bowl of oil, let his mind wander outside?" - "Bhikkhus, I give this simile to convey the meaning. And this is the meaning: 'The bowl filled with oil' is a synonym for mindfulness of the body. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will develop mindfulness of the body, cultivate it, make it our vehicle, make it our base, establish it, accumulate it, and properly undertake it.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families,…
content: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding praise, and causing donated goods to be wasted. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in heaven. What five? No stinginess regarding dwellings, no stinginess regarding families, no stinginess regarding gains, no stinginess regarding praise, and not causing donated goods to be wasted. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in heaven.

title: - Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful? Here, bhikkhus,…
content: - Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world ... Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu clearly comprehending? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu knows feelings as they arise, knows feelings as they persist, knows feelings as they pass away; knows perceptions as they arise, knows perceptions as they persist, knows perceptions as they pass away. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu clearly comprehending. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you.
